name: State
description: Data that a component owns and manages internally, which can change over time and causes the component to re-render when updated.
notes: Unlike props, state is local to the component and controlled by that component (or lifted to a parent), not passed in from outside.

name: Lifting State Up
description: Moving shared state to the closest common ancestor of the components that need it, then passing it back down via props, so multiple components stay in sync.

name: State vs Props
description: Props are passed in from a parent and are read-only from the receiving component's perspective; state is owned and can be updated by the component itself.
notes: A component re-renders when either its own state changes or the props it receives change.

name: Immutability of State
description: State must be updated by creating a new value (new object/array) rather than mutating the existing one in place, so React can detect the change and re-render.
notes: Mutating state directly (e.g. `arr.push()`, `obj.prop = x`) can silently fail to trigger a re-render because React compares references, not deep equality.

name: Batched State Updates
description: React groups multiple `setState` calls triggered within the same event handler (and, since React 18, in most other contexts too) into a single re-render for performance.
notes: Use the functional updater form (`setCount(c => c + 1)`) when a new value depends on the previous one, since batched updates can make reading the outer variable stale.

name: Derived State Anti-Pattern
description: Storing a value in state that could instead be computed directly from existing props/state during render, which leads to state going out of sync with its source.
notes: If a value can be calculated from props/state during render, compute it inline (or with useMemo for expensive calculations) instead of duplicating it into its own state.

name: Lazy Initial State
description: Passing a function to `useState` so the initial value is computed only once, on the first render, instead of being recalculated on every render.
notes: Useful when computing the initial value is expensive; passing `useState(expensiveParse(rawData))` directly would run that computation on every render even though only the first result is used.

name: Local vs Global State
description: Local state lives in a single component (or is lifted to a nearby parent); global state is accessible application-wide, typically via Context or a state management library.
notes: Prefer local state by default and only reach for global state when data genuinely needs to be shared across distant, unrelated parts of the tree.
